svg.text: talk.01 · v0.5 study · TONE-ON-TONE COLOUR AND OUR OWN LETTERING
body and lid in one colour family, only a bright key · a hand-drawn wordmark and a pixel-dot label font made for this device
TENTATIVE · NOT A FINAL DESIGN
front views at 10 mm = 40 px
WARM
warm grey body, a shade deeper
plate, orange key
GRAPHITE
charcoal body, a shade deeper plate,
amber key
SAGE
sage body, a deeper sage plate, red
key
OUR OWN LETTERING
the wordmark is drawn, not typed: one stroke weight, round ends, an open bowl, the dot, 0 and 1 in the accent colour
W1 · stroke 1.15 mm, 6 mm tall (on the fronts)
W2 · stroke 1.9 mm: chunkier
THE LABEL FONT (5 x 7 dots, drawn here as squares and as dots)
What the lettering has to respect (FDM):
· a 0.4 mm nozzle prints lines of about 0.8 mm or more. The wordmark (1.15
mm strokes) can be raised or engraved; the pixel labels at 2 mm tall
cannot, so they are decals, UV print or paint-filled engraving. If they
must be printed, use cells of 0.7 mm and a text 5 mm tall (a few big words
only).
· the font is original: 5 x 7 dot letters drawn for this project (no third-
party font). The wordmark is hand-drawn too.
Tone-on-tone, in short:
· the key is the only loud thing; the body and lid stay in one family, the
lid a shade deeper so the seam reads;
· the wheel is the dark (or the light) part, as the pair of the key; the
dot, the 0 and the 1 carry the key's colour.
· all three palettes also work with the red lamp; the lamp is the second
spot of colour.
